metadata.title: General Listings Marketplace Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how a local listings marketplace would need to change when it becomes accountable for unsafe goods, fraudsters manufacture convincing people and listings, ranking rules constrain personalization and paid visibility, or one promoted recalled item combines all three pressures.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A seller creates an account and listing, the marketplace classifies and ranks it, buyers discover it, message the seller, and either arrange an off-platform handoff or use protected payment and shipping. The design assumes the listing describes a lawful item, an account represents a reasonably stable actor, and ranking and promotion may use available behavior and seller spend.
metadata.residualArchitecture: The changed design separates actor, identity evidence, account, role, listing, physical item, product identity, safety status, jurisdiction, policy, moderation decision, interaction, channel, transaction protection, ranking candidate, ranking reason, paid placement, and consent. This lets the marketplace withdraw unsafe supply, challenge synthetic actors, preserve safe communication, and explain discovery without binding trust or visibility to one account score or opaque rank.
metadata.note: The tests begin outside the software: product-safety law, an adversarial fraud economy, and limits on marketplace ranking power. The architectural change is a traceable chain from real actor and item to policy, decision, exposure, conversation, and transaction.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: A product-safety law makes the marketplace responsible for recalled and prohibited goods
stressors.detection: Final law and guidance, official recall and prohibited-goods feeds, manufacturer identifiers, listing content, seller documents, buyer reports, moderation decisions, transactions, and regulator notices.
stressors.attractor: A free-text listing can no longer be treated only as seller speech. The marketplace must know what physical item is offered, which rules apply in its location and category, whether it is recalled, who supplied it, who saw or bought it, and how quickly exposure was stopped.
stressors.businessReaction: Identify affected supply, stop new publication and promotion, withdraw active listings, notify sellers and exposed buyers, pause protected transactions, preserve evidence, support refunds or safe disposal where required, and prove the action to authorities without blocking unrelated recommerce.
stressors.residue: Separate listing from physical item, normalized product identity, category, jurisdiction, seller assertion, supporting evidence, safety notice, policy version, moderation decision, exposure, conversation, and transaction. A new safety fact can suspend every affected listing and downstream action while retaining appeal, notification, refund, and audit state.

impacts.effect: Easy household selling includes guided product identification and safety checks before exposure to buyers.
Sellers can create a trustworthy listing with clear evidence and correction paths for regulated items.
Publication and monitoring react to changing product-safety status after the listing goes live.
Dispute-free completion excludes sales later invalidated by a recall or prohibited-goods decision.
Adds product-safety intake, affected-listing discovery, exposure control, notification, redress, and regulator evidence.
Identifies the actual product and applicable market rules without turning ordinary listing into a legal research task.
Links category attributes and product identifiers to recalls, restrictions, and required evidence.
Versions listing publication, suspension, correction, withdrawal, appeal, and notification state.
Preserves seller evidence, authority notices, decision records, and redress documents.
Owns product-safety policy with category, seller, legal, operations, payments, communications, and regulator teams.
Makes cross-category recall response and buyer redress a mature recommerce benchmark.

stressors.name: Fraud networks use synthetic identities, copied inventory, and convincing generated voice and video
stressors.detection: Identity and device evidence, copied media and text, graph overlap, account behavior, message and link patterns, reports, payment destinations, call metadata, delivery evidence, disputes, and law-enforcement intelligence.
stressors.attractor: A polished profile, realistic video, long account history, and apparently unique listing no longer establish that a person controls the item. Fraudsters build many disposable roles, earn trust, move buyers to external channels, redirect payment, and reappear after one account is removed.
stressors.businessReaction: Challenge higher-consequence actors and actions, identify coordinated networks, warn before unsafe channel changes, preserve buyer choice, offer protected transaction paths, slow or stop suspicious reach and payout, investigate linked cases, and provide recovery evidence without assuming every new seller is fraudulent.
stressors.residue: Separate human or organization, presented identity, verified evidence, account, device, role, listing control claim, media provenance, contact endpoint, conversation, external-channel transition, payment destination, transaction, trust decision, challenge, and case. Trust is contextual to an action and can survive account replacement or expose coordinated identities.

impacts.effect: Buyer confidence comes from action-specific evidence and protected choices rather than polished profile appearance.
Buyers can negotiate and complete a local transaction while understanding identity, item-control, channel, and payment warnings.
The trust check explains verified facts, unresolved claims, unsafe channel changes, and available protection.
Fraud reporting follows coordinated actor and transaction outcomes rather than counting only removed accounts.
Adds actor-network investigation, media provenance, action challenges, channel warnings, destination controls, and linked recovery cases.
Carries contextual trust and protection from discovery through conversation, payment, handoff, and dispute.
Stores evidence and verification scope separately from account identity and re-challenges consequential changes.
Scores the actor, role, relationship, and action graph rather than one disposable account.
Detects risky channel and payment transitions and preserves conversation evidence with proportionate privacy controls.
Owns reusable actor and action trust with messaging, listing, payments, safety operations, privacy, and recovery teams.
Makes defense against synthetic local-commerce actors and off-platform diversion a key marketplace benchmark.

stressors.name: New marketplace rules prohibit opaque behavioral ranking and require paid placement to be explainable
stressors.detection: Final regulation and enforcement, consent changes, ranking and advertising audits, seller complaints, buyer research, experiment results, paid-placement contracts, and regulator information requests.
stressors.attractor: Personalized discovery and paid visibility drive liquidity and revenue, but the platform cannot explain why one listing outranked another or prove that behavioral data and seller spend were used lawfully. Removing ranking entirely harms relevance; preserving it unchanged undermines buyer choice and seller fairness.
stressors.businessReaction: Define permitted ranking purposes and inputs, label paid influence, give buyers meaningful controls, provide sellers understandable performance evidence, preserve non-personalized discovery, audit changes, and redesign monetization around demonstrable value instead of hidden reach manipulation.
stressors.residue: Separate discovery request, buyer intent, consent, eligible candidate set, organic signals, personalization signals, policy version, ranking decision, explanation, paid campaign, placement influence, experiment, exposure, and outcome. The same inventory can be ranked through different lawful modes without mixing paid and organic evidence.

impacts.effect: Professional sellers buy understandable merchandising value rather than unexplained preferential treatment.
Merchants can operate inventory and visibility with clear organic, paid, contextual, and personalized performance.
Campaign setup and reporting show placement rules, paid influence, eligible audience, explanation, and measured outcome.
Visibility ROI confidence depends on traceable exposure and outcome, separated from organic demand.
Adds explainable promotion modes, buyer controls, seller evidence, lawful experiments, and auditable attribution.
Keeps merchandising and paid visibility usable under transparent ranking and consent constraints.
Separates campaign eligibility, budget, placement influence, exposure, and attributed outcome.
Records candidate set, permitted signals, policy, rank, paid influence, and buyer-facing explanation.
Controls allowed discovery purposes, consent, retention, access, and non-personalized alternatives.
Owns transparent seller value with discovery, monetization, privacy, analytics, legal, and buyer-experience teams.
Makes explainable local-market ranking and paid visibility a European classifieds benchmark.

stressors.name: A synthetic dealer promotes a recalled high-demand product to buyers who disabled behavioral tracking
stressors.detection: Recall feed, normalized product match, actor and account graph, identity challenges, copied listing media, ranking policy, buyer consent, paid campaign, exposure records, conversations, protected transactions, and reports.
stressors.attractor: The listing looks credible, the seller has manufactured trust, paid promotion expands reach, and the affected buyers cannot be identified through unrestricted behavioral profiles. Account removal alone leaves copied supply, unsafe exposure, buyer contact, and redress unresolved.
stressors.businessReaction: Stop the affected item and campaign, challenge the actor network, find exposure through purpose-limited event records, warn contacted buyers, pause or reverse protected transactions, support appeals and refunds, and report the recall action without reconstructing unrelated buyer behavior.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: normalized product and safety records withdraw every affected listing, actor-level trust links synthetic accounts and payment destinations, and explainable purpose-bound exposure records identify recall communication without restoring opaque behavioral profiling.

impacts.effect: Buyer safety survives the combination of unsafe supply, convincing fraud, paid reach, and privacy limits.
Discovery can remove unsafe inventory and explain prior exposure without depending on a hidden behavioral profile.
Saved and contacted listings carry withdrawal reason, seller status, transaction action, and safe alternatives.
Trust-safe transaction rate includes recall detection, exposure response, fraud linkage, and completed redress.
Composes item, actor, campaign, consent, exposure, communication, transaction, and outcome evidence for response.
Reuses governed product, trust, ranking, and exposure data to coordinate the recall without new surveillance.
Links the synthetic actor network and suspicious payment destinations behind the recalled inventory.
Preserves buyer consent and the permitted safety-communication purpose separately from advertising tracking.
Sends recall and redress messages from purpose-limited exposure and transaction records.
Coordinates governed response data across safety, identity, discovery, messaging, payments, seller, and support teams.
Makes privacy-preserving cross-category recall and fraud response a horizontal marketplace benchmark.
